sources.applicability: Primary evidence: (a) open defect #25824 — CSV sniffer fixes column types from first sample_size rows (default 20,480 lines); values beyond the sample are silently rounded/truncated (1.5->2, timestamps lose time-of-day, leading zeros and _ separators absorbed) while the sniffer itself would reject them, because sniffer and scanner use different cast strictness; sample_size=-1 and all_varchar=true recover correct behavior; store_rejects=true records zero rejects because no error is raised; reporter's version matrix shows the behavior across 1.1.3, 1.5.5, 1.6.0.dev214 nightly and main@2bbfe6f236 (v2.1.0-dev). (b) closed defect #15777 — COPY fails when dateformat='AUTO' is set explicitly by the user but succeeds when AUTO is auto-detected; DuckDB 1.1.3. Limits: open issue = no fix yet; issue bodies are reporter claims plus maintainer labels ('reproduced' on 15777/15576), not release documentation.

sources.exact_locator: 'NBClient lets you execute notebooks... A client library for programmatic notebook execution'; 'Python Version Support: This library currently supports Python 3.10+ versions'; 'NBClient extracted nbconvert's ExecutePreprocessor into its own library'; Relationship section: 'jupyter_client ... provides the Python API for starting, managing and communicating with Jupyter kernels. sources.applicability: Clean-replay precedent: programmatic whole-notebook execution exists as a maintained library separate from the interactive UI, and the kernel-protocol client is a separate layer. sources.exact_locator: section 'Security in the Jupyter Server', first paragraph: 'Since access to the Jupyter Server means access to running arbitrary code, it is important to restrict access to the server.'
sources.capture_identity: capture_id 035d0a8c0d504b39a4810ca07f86180c; partial_capture (79,569 bytes captured, first 32,768 readable); cited sentence is inside the readable range
sources.applicability: The Jupyter project's own threat model: notebook/server access equals arbitrary code execution. Supports the design rule that the execution boundary must be an OS/process boundary, never an import blacklist. The page itself addresses server authentication, not kernel sandboxing — sandboxing is left to the operator/OS layer (engineering inference from its scope).

sources.applicability: Vendor documentation of the exact knobs this design maps to data-contract controls: sampled type inference (preview != full-dataset proof), reject capture instead of silent deletion, explicit schema override, schema alignment across files, and stable (insertion) vs unspecified ordering. Versioned with the 'current' docs tree (1.5 line per S10 render).
